title: Promote tricep recovery & hypertrophy in less than 2 minutes!
summary: NH demonstrates a band triceps extension drop-set: band anchored at chest height, grip high enough to be challenging, extend without locking the elbows, and slide the grip down as it gets hard until no resistance remains. He recommends 3-4 sets on lower-body day (between squat sets) to pump blood into the elbow for recovery and some triceps growth.

claims.claim: A band triceps extension isolates the triceps and sends blood into the muscle, helping alleviate tendinitis and elbow pain, with almost no equipment and in very little time.
Setup: tie a band around a post at chest level and grab it high enough that the extension is challenging but not a struggle.
When reps get too hard, loosen the grip and slide down the band to reduce resistance and keep going, until there is no resistance left.
Never lock the elbow on extensions; keep the tension on the muscle.
Even without shoulder flexion, NH feels this movement strongly in the long head of the triceps.
Do it on lower-body day, e.g. between squat sets, not on upper-body day where it would burn out the triceps; use it on days without pushing movements.
Sending blood in and around the joint helps push nutrients in and speeds recovery.
NH gets a better triceps pump from this in under a minute than he usually gets from skull crushers; do 3-4 sets for elbow health and some size.
